      "text": "(A). Path II: a bimolecular oxidative addition of [Ni IL*X] ( A)\nwith aryl bromides initiates the reaction to provide D, wherein\ncomplex A is regenerated by the reduction of nickel( II) complex\nB with zinc. Thereafter, reduction of D with zinc a ﬀords the\naryl-nickel(I) complex ( H), which reacts with tertiary alkyl\nbromide via a SET pathway to produce D and the tertiary alkyl\nradical. As before, alkyl radical F is generated from 1,3-enyne\nand the tertiary alkyl radical. Combination of D and F provides\nthe pivotal chiral intermediate G. Finally, reductive elimination\nof G aﬀords the chiral product and regenerates A. These\nmechanistic insights highlight the role of chiral ligands in\ncontrolling the reactions of chiral key intermediates and chiral\nproducts, further validating the proposed catalytic cycle.\nConclusions\nIn summary, we have developed an e ﬃcient synthetic route for\nasymmetric tetrasubstituted allenes, demonstrating the suc-\ncessful application of mechanochemistry in asymmetric\nnickel-catalyzed reductive coupling reactions. This study is the\nfirst report of an asymmetric three-component nickel-catalyzed\nreductive coupling reaction using ball-milling techniques.\nWhile the enantioselectivities obtained represent significant\nprogress for this challenging transformation, ongoing e ﬀorts\nare focused on further optimization of ee values through\nligand design and reaction engineering. Overall, this innova-\ntive mechanochemical protocol provides a more e ﬃcient and\npractical approach for asymmetric radical reductive coupling,\nwith significant potential for a wide range of applications in\norganic synthesis.\nAuthor contributions\nHao Lei: investigation; conceptualization; methodology; and\nwriting – original draft. Yufang Yang: methodology. Jiajia Sun:\nmethodology. Shu Fan: methodology. Xiaofeng Wei: formal\nanalysis; supervision; and writing – review & editing. Siyuan\nWang: investigation; methodology; and project administration.\nHai-Shu Lin: project administration and writing – review &\nediting. Yan Kang: conceptualization; project administration;\nsupervision; and writing – review & editing.\nConﬂicts of interest\nThere are no conflicts to declare.\nData availability\nThe data supporting this article have been included as part of\nthe ESI.†\nAcknowledgement\nWe thank the Natural Science Foundation of Top Talent of\nSZTU (grant No. GDRC202122), Featured Innovation\nFoundation of Ordinary Higher Education Institutions of\nGuangdong Province (grant No.2021KTSCX112), High-Level\nIntroduction Plan of Shaanxi Province (71240000000111),\nNatural Science Foundation of Shaanxi Province (2022JM-085,\n2022JQ-121), the start-up funds from Xi ’an Jiaotong University\n(XJTU).\nReferences\n1 S.
